LA-2026-HB159.aiSummary: Creates a pilot program in Caddo Parish that would let the sheriff use active electronic monitoring as an alternative to jail for some eligible defendants before trial. It would require written rules, risk checks, monthly mental health checks for some people, and approval from the court, sheriff, and district attorney before someone joins. The law also sets rules for electronic monitoring providers, funding, reporting, and limits when the sheriff or parish can be held responsible for harm caused by a participant, and it became law on June 9, 2026.

LA-2026-HB1117.aiSummary: The law changes how some insurance payments affect the time limit for filing a claim. It says an insurer’s payment under certain policy terms does not count as an admission of debt or extend that time limit, and it requires written notice of that for some homeowners’ claims. The new rule on some parts takes effect January 1, 2027; the rest took effect when the governor signed it.
